overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law: the Chair's December 14, 2015 email, copied to the other two members, was deliberation outside a noticed meeting. The conflicting claim about a post-meeting statement was not decided.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee discussed a vacant Fire Commissioner seat and the resignation outside a noticed meeting, including by email among members.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the December 14, 2015 e-mail sent by the Chair, on which the other two Committee members were copied, constituted deliberation outside of a noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a member told the public after the December 21 meeting that he had heard about the resignation from the Chair, a private discussion outside a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Based on these conflicting versions of events, we make no finding with respect to this allegation.

allegations.summary: To the extent the complaint said the Committee was obligated to discuss the Commissioner's resignation, the AG addressed whether the law requires discussing any topic.
allegations.key_passage: we note that the Open Meeting Law does not obligate a public body to discuss any topic.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Review the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law Guide and certify in writing to this office, within 30 days of receipt, that members have reviewed the determination and the Guide.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. Additionally, we order the Committee to review the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law Guide, available at www.mass.gov/ago/openmeeting and to certify in writing to this office, using the attached form, within thirty (30) days of receipt of this letter that its members have reviewed this determination and the Guide.
